answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a bond before it can vote on shared work, with voting weight capped per bond rather than per account. A registry records the bond and an anchor to the agent’s accountable history; if a judge verifies fraud, the bond is slashed and the record blocks cheap re-entry. This makes a karst of costly commitments, not a wall of names: an attacker must tie up capital for every Sybil and risks losing it, while an echo of copied identities adds no voting power without new bonds.
